2007-07-10: EU finance ministers agree to back Dominique Strauss-Kahn as the next managing director of the IMF, while Britain refuses to abide by the decision.
2007-07-12: The IMF board agreed to an open selection process for its top job, with developing countries demanding that Dominique Strauss-Kahn, backed by most European countries, not stand unopposed.
2007-08-25: Dominique Strauss-Kahn is all but certain to clinch the top job at the International Monetary Fund after nominations close this week, despite calls from developing countries for a candidate from outside Europe.
2008-04-10: IMF Managing Director Dominique Strauss-Kahn said the global economy is caught between a sharp slowdown and rising inflation, ahead of a G7 finance ministers meeting.
2008-10-17: Dominique Strauss-Kahn, the head of the International Monetary Fund, is under investigation for allegedly abusing his position by engaging in a sexual relationship with a senior official.
2008-10-18: The IMF begins an inquiry into whether Dominique Strauss-Kahn abused his position through a sexual relationship with a subordinate, a charge he denies.
2011-05-09: Dominique Strauss-Kahn, head of the IMF and a potential Socialist presidential candidate, faces a political headache after being photographed climbing into a €100,000 Porsche, dubbed "Porschegate," which threatens his efforts to shed a champagne-socialist image.
2011-05-10: Dominique Strauss-Kahn received a satirical award at the "Les Gerard" ceremony, based partly on his reputation for womanizing.
2011-05-13: Dominique Strauss-Kahn is in Rikers Island prison facing charges of sexual assault on a 32-year-old chambermaid, and denies committing the assault at his Manhattan hotel.
2011-05-14: Dominique Strauss-Kahn was detained in New York on accusations he tried to rape a hotel maid and told police he had diplomatic immunity.
Dominique Strauss-Kahn, head of the International Monetary Fund, was arrested and charged with sexually assaulting and attempting to rape a maid in a New York hotel.
2011-05-15: Dominique Strauss-Kahn was arrested and detained in New York on charges of sexual assault, prompting IMF board discussions about his position.
Dominique Strauss-Kahn was arrested and charged with the attempted rape of a 32-year-old chambermaid in New York.
Further allegations of sexual assault against Dominique Strauss-Kahn were broadcast on French television, with a Socialist party official claiming he attacked her daughter, Tristane Banon, in 2002.
2011-05-16: Dominique Strauss-Kahn faces allegations of attempted rape and sexual assault, including a planned police complaint by Tristane Banon, which he denies.
IMF chief Dominique Strauss-Kahn is arrested over the weekend, an event analysts say adds uncertainty to markets but is unlikely to obstruct progress on Portuguese or Greek bailout packages.
Dominique Strauss-Kahn's arrest on rape charges leads to his anticipated departure as IMF managing director and sparks a race to succeed him.
A New York judge refused bail and ordered IMF chief Dominique Strauss-Kahn remanded in custody on charges of sexually assaulting a hotel maid.
2011-05-17: US treasury secretary Tim Geithner and European finance ministers question whether Dominique Strauss-Kahn can continue as IMF head following his arrest, with Geithner saying Strauss-Kahn is "obviously not in a position to run the IMF."
Dominique Strauss-Kahn's arrest on sexual assault charges sparks a national debate in France about sex, power, and the treatment of his accuser by his political allies.
2011-05-18: Dominique Strauss-Kahn resigned as managing director of the International Monetary Fund to focus on defending himself against sexual assault charges in New York.
The head of the IMF, Dominique Strauss-Kahn, was arrested in New York, with potentially huge effects on the global response to running economic crises.
Dominique Strauss-Kahn resigned from his position as managing director of the International Monetary Fund following his arrest on charges of attempted rape and sexual assault.
French philosopher Bernard-Henri Lévy publishes a piece defending Dominique Strauss-Kahn, stressing that the accusations of attempted rape against him have not been proven.
2011-05-19: Dominique Strauss-Kahn's lawyers are set to offer new bail terms, including $1 million in cash and house arrest, at a fresh bail hearing.

The alleged victim is expected to testify before a grand jury deciding whether to prosecute Dominique Strauss-Kahn, who is hoping to be granted bail as his lawyers return to court to contest charges of sexual assault and attempted rape.
Former IMF chief Dominique Strauss-Kahn is granted bail by a New York court under house arrest with armed guard while facing trial for allegedly sexually assaulting a Manhattan hotel maid.
2011-05-20: Dominique Strauss-Kahn was granted bail and barred from moving into an exclusive New York apartment, instead staying in a corporate apartment under house arrest while facing charges of attempted rape.
2011-05-24: DNA tests reportedly confirmed a link between Dominique Strauss-Kahn and material found on the hotel maid's uniform in the alleged sexual assault case.
2011-06-06: Dominique Strauss-Kahn denied attempted rape and sexual assault of a hotel maid at a Manhattan criminal court hearing.
Hotel workers protested outside a courthouse as Dominique Strauss-Kahn arrived for his arraignment on charges of attempted rape and unlawful imprisonment.
2011-06-07: The contest to succeed Dominique Strauss-Kahn as IMF managing director intensifies as Mexico's Agustín Carstens criticizes Europe for seeking to impose Christine Lagarde on the rest of the world.
2011-06-28: Dominique Strauss-Kahn exited political life amid attempted rape charges in the US, prompting Martine Aubry to enter the French Socialist presidential race.
2011-07-01: Reports that the New York prosecution case for alleged sexual assault against Dominique Strauss-Kahn could be close to collapse stun France and revive hopes that he may return to politics.
Dominique Strauss-Kahn was freed from house arrest and had his bail dropped after prosecutors discovered his accuser had lied about a previous rape claim and other key elements of her account.
2011-07-02: French Socialists were in chaos as key figures speculated whether Dominique Strauss-Kahn could return to challenge Nicolas Sarkozy in the 2012 presidential race, despite still facing seven charges including attempted rape.
2011-07-04: French writer Tristane Banon announced she was filing a lawsuit against Dominique Strauss-Kahn for attempted rape, and Strauss-Kahn responded that he would sue her for defamation.
2011-07-05: The hotel maid at the centre of the attempted rape case against Dominique Strauss-Kahn sues the New York Post for libel after the newspaper accused her of working as a prostitute.
2011-07-19: Lawyers for the two women accusing Dominique Strauss-Kahn of attempted rape met for the first time in New York, raising the prospect that they will join forces to strengthen their cases against the former IMF chief.
2011-07-24: Nafissatou Diallo, the hotel worker who accused Dominique Strauss-Kahn of sexual assault, revealed her identity and gave interviews to Newsweek and ABC News detailing her allegations.
2011-08-16: Prosecutors are expected to drop sexual assault and other charges against Dominique Strauss-Kahn at a court hearing on Tuesday.
2011-08-22: French writer Tristane Banon remains determined to pursue her claim that Dominique Strauss-Kahn attempted to rape her in 2003, after New York prosecutors dropped separate sexual assault charges against him.
French Socialists indicate that Dominique Strauss-Kahn could return to politics if sexual assault charges against him in New York are dropped.
2011-08-23: A New York judge dismissed the criminal sexual assault charges against Dominique Strauss-Kahn after prosecutors said they could not prove the case beyond a reasonable doubt due to credibility issues with his accuser.
2011-08-26: French Socialists at their La Rochelle conference express fear that Dominique Strauss-Kahn might return to politics after New York prosecutors dropped all charges against him, with a poll finding 80% of people do not want him to play any role in the Socialist primary race.
2011-09-04: Dominique Strauss-Kahn returns to Paris after sexual assault charges against him were dropped, facing separate questioning by Paris police over an allegation that he attempted to rape writer Tristane Banon in 2003.
2011-09-12: Dominique Strauss-Kahn was questioned by French police investigating a second attempted rape allegation made by novelist and journalist Tristane Banon.
2011-09-18: Dominique Strauss-Kahn gave a TV interview that stoked tensions among French Socialists by confirming a political "pact" with Martine Aubry and making off-the-record comments about the primary race.
2011-09-26: Dominique Strauss-Kahn asked a New York judge to dismiss the civil suit filed by hotel maid Nafissatou Diallo, arguing he was immune under international law.
2011-10-09: Dominique Strauss-Kahn, the former IMF head and expected leading Socialist candidate, had dropped out of the French presidential race after being accused of attempting to rape a chambermaid in New York, and he voted in the Socialist party's primary for Martine Aubry.
2011-10-13: French writer Tristane Banon, who accused Dominique Strauss-Kahn of attempted rape in 2003, publishes a book in which she appears to refer to him as a "baboon."
2011-11-11: Dominique Strauss-Kahn demanded to be interviewed by investigative judges in the Lille Hotel Carlton prostitution-ring case, denouncing a "media lynching" after his name was linked to the investigation.
2011-12-27: Director Abel Ferrara is working on a film about political sex scandals partly inspired by Dominique Strauss-Kahn, with Gérard Depardieu and Isabelle Adjani in talks to star.
2012-02-06: Gerard Depardieu is set to take the lead role in Abel Ferrara's Dominique Strauss-Kahn-inspired film about political sex scandals.
2012-02-14: Dominique Strauss-Kahn is to be questioned by French police investigating an alleged prostitution ring.
2012-02-21: Dominique Strauss-Kahn was formally placed under arrest by French police investigating an alleged prostitution ring.
2012-03-09: Dominique Strauss-Kahn is set to address the Cambridge Union Society, with protesting students planning a demonstration outside the building.
2012-03-26: A French judge charged former IMF head Dominique Strauss-Kahn over alleged links with a prostitution ring, placing him under formal investigation for "complicity in aggravated and organised prostitution" and "misuse of company assets."
2012-03-28: Lawyers for Nafissatou Diallo argued in Bronx supreme court that Dominique Strauss-Kahn's claim of immunity from her civil lawsuit is "completely baseless," as a judge adjourned to consider his verdict.
2012-04-13: Dominique Strauss-Kahn gives his first major newspaper interview since his 2011 arrest, claiming his downfall was orchestrated to derail his French presidential ambitions.
2012-04-27: Nicolas Sarkozy challenged Dominique Strauss-Kahn to take legal action over Strauss-Kahn's allegations that Sarkozy-linked individuals orchestrated the scandal that ended his political career.
2012-04-29: The French Socialist party distanced itself from Dominique Strauss-Kahn after he alleged that political enemies linked to Nicolas Sarkozy's party helped discredit him over the New York hotel housekeeper accusation.
2012-05-01: A New York judge ruled that a hotel maid's civil lawsuit accusing Dominique Strauss-Kahn of sexual assault can proceed to trial, rejecting his claim of diplomatic immunity.
2012-05-22: Dominique Strauss-Kahn's accuser in a civil sexual assault lawsuit added new claims that the alleged attack amounted to gender violence.
2012-06-07: A new book claims Dominique Strauss-Kahn's womanising was well known in Parisian political circles and that some, including Francois Hollande and Nicolas Sarkozy, never thought he could run for president.
2012-10-02: French prosecutors dropped a preliminary inquiry into whether Dominique Strauss-Kahn could face rape charges over the alleged group rape of a Belgian sex worker, though he remains under formal investigation over alleged complicity in a pimping operation.
2012-12-10: Dominique Strauss-Kahn settled a civil sexual assault lawsuit with hotel maid Nafissatou Diallo for a confidential sum, ending her New York court battle against him.
2012-12-11: Dominique Strauss-Kahn settles a lawsuit with a New York hotel maid.
2013-02-26: Dominique Strauss-Kahn seeks an injunction in a French court to block a kiss-and-tell memoir by former lover Marcela Iacub, seeking a ban on distribution, damages, and an inserted notice.
2013-05-16: The first images from Abel Ferrara's feature film inspired by the Dominique Strauss-Kahn scandal, starring Gérard Depardieu, are released ahead of a showing at the Cannes film festival.
2013-07-26: French magistrates decided that Dominique Strauss-Kahn will stand trial on a charge of aggravated pimping as part of a group in connection with an alleged prostitution ring at a Lille hotel.
2015-02-02: Dominique Strauss-Kahn appeared in court in Lille for the start of his trial on charges of aggravated pimping, which he has denied.
2015-02-04: The Hotel Carlton pimping trial in Lille hears testimony about prostitution, with defendant Dominique Strauss-Kahn, the ex-head of the IMF, accused of aiding and abetting prostitution by having group sex with paid women; he strongly denies the pimping charge.
2015-02-10: Dominique Strauss-Kahn denied committing any crime as his trial began in Lille, France, on charges of aggravated pimping for allegedly aiding and abetting the prostitution of seven women.
2015-02-11: In court, a second woman, Jade, testified that Dominique Strauss-Kahn subjected her to a sex act against her will, during his trial in Lille on aggravated pimping charges.
2015-02-12: Dominique Strauss-Kahn told a French court that he rented a luxury Paris flat under an acquaintance's name because he was married and wanted a discreet place to meet women for group sex, as he stands trial on charges of aggravated pimping, which he denies.
2015-02-14: Dominique Strauss-Kahn defends himself in a French court against charges of pimping.
2015-03-20: Abel Ferrara threatens to sue US distributors over a version of his film about the Dominique Strauss-Kahn scandal, Welcome to New York, that was re-edited without his involvement.
2015-03-23: IFC Films disputes Abel Ferrara’s claims over the US edit of his film Welcome to New York, which is based on the Dominique Strauss-Kahn scandal, saying Ferrara refused to engage in producing an R-rated version.
2015-06-12: Dominique Strauss-Kahn was acquitted on charges of aggravated pimping, though public opinion in France continues to condemn him.
2015-08-17: Warner Bros is developing a film titled The Libertine, a comedic dramatisation based on the Dominique Strauss-Kahn sexual assault scandal, with no casting or director yet announced.
2016-05-11: Johnny Depp and Marion Cotillard are set to star in a Dominique Strauss-Kahn-inspired drama titled The Libertine for director Brett Ratner.
